review.summary: The wire chunk is minimal, well-evidenced and honest. profiles.rs changes exactly two request-schema arguments (lines 91, 214) with frozen response roots and identical `.named()` ids, proven byte-exactly against baseline 578f2e6. Directional wire tests drive create/update/list_for_token/list/get/paged list_all under both response policies, reject 5 pointers x 3 invalid values pre-auth (token.calls 0, wire.requests 0), and round-trip raw extensions plus unknown direction keys. Both attempt-4 lows are fixed with enforcing regressions. All 107 recorded checks exit 0 on source 93d22ec2 in one contiguous 09:53-10:11 run, including both compilers, the executed example, dependency audit ordered first, and native export probes. One low remains: the operation ledger attributes a list-only test to create/update/get.

findings.description: The create row (line 633), update row (line 785) and get row (line 689) all cite crates/scm-sdk/tests/management_contracts.rs::profile_wire_defaults_and_empty_terminal_pages_follow_request_options as contract evidence, but that test (management_contracts.rs:1985-2044) only calls list_for_token, list and list_all; it never invokes create, update or get. The over-attribution propagates into contracts/qualification.json:13946, contracts/native-operations.json and contracts/native-exports.json, and tools/test_typescript035_profiles.py:31-32 actively requires it by iterating all four WIRE_TESTS for create/update.
findings.required_fix: Bind profile_wire_defaults_and_empty_terminal_pages_follow_request_options only to the listForToken/list/listAll rows, drop it from the create/update/get rows, regenerate native-operations.json, native-exports.json and qualification.json, and narrow the assertion in tools/test_typescript035_profiles.py to the tests each operation actually exercises.

evidence: crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/management/profiles.rs:91,214 are the only changed schema arguments ("typescript:0.35.0:CreateSecurityProfileRequestSchema"); response roots at 76,92,107,215,231 and the delete/force_delete paths are untouched. tools/test_typescript035_implementation.py:67-76 proves this mechanically against baseline 578f2e6 (before.count==2, after.count==2, after.replace(current,previous)==before, identical .named() lists).

crates/scm-sdk/tests/management_contracts.rs:1725-1733 defines a fixture carrying all four directions plus an unknown "future-direction" key; 1736-1839 drives POST /v1/mgmt/profile, PUT /v1/mgmt/profile/uuid/{ID}, list_for_token, list, get and a 2-page list_all for defaults true and false against a reply with null dlp_tenant_id, integer tool-call and null enable-full-conversation-inspection, asserting byte-equal serde round-trips. This proves the response root stays tolerant on the real wire path.

crates/scm-sdk/tests/management_contracts.rs:1842-1873 sends 5 JSON pointers x 3 invalid values (null, 17, array) through create and update asserting ErrorKind::Validation with token.calls==0 and wire.requests==0, and constructs them via the still-available historical passthrough root (line 1858). Lines 1876-1982 prove raw .extension() requests serialize identically and decode into typed projections, including nested tool-response app-protection, under both response modes.

docs/reviews/phase-27-chunk-wire-and-compatibility-attempt-05.checks.json: phase 27, passed true, source_sha256 93d22ec2 equal to the reviewed source, 107 commands, zero non-zero exit codes, no timeouts, every source_unchanged true, all executed_at inside 2026-10-22T09:53:19-10:11:30 with no reused checkpoint prefix. tools/review_phase.py:215 enforces that the recorded command list equals commands_for(27) and 220-221 re-verifies checkpoint bindings for current source.

Receipt lines 2958-3021: scripts/check-rust.py on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 for the management feature set runs fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, test, test --examples, doc and cargo run --example directional_profiles, all exit 0. scripts/check-rust.py:73-75 wires that example run and crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:83-85 gates it behind required-features=["management"], asserted by tools/test_ci.py:515-517.

Attempt-4 low 1 fixed: docs/LIVE_ACCEPTANCE.md:23 now states "Directional profile create/update remain live-unverified." in the current read-only section, and tools/test_live_acceptance_docs.py:32 asserts that exact sentence.

Attempt-4 low 2 partly fixed: contracts/native-operation-mappings/management.json:686-690, 724-728, 742-746, 762-766 add directional read-path tests to get/list/listAll/listForToken, with tools/test_typescript035_profiles.py:33-38 asserting them; the directional test name appears consistently in native-operations.json (6), qualification.json (12) and native-exports.json (19), so regeneration is coherent.

Dependency advisories: tools/test_typescript035_implementation.py:90-110 proves the lockfile changed only rustls-webpki 0.103.15->0.103.16 and webpki-root-certs 1.0.9->1.0.10 (same package count, same order, new checksums) and that scripts/check-dependencies.py precedes the first check-rust in commands_for(27); the receipt confirms that order (audit at line 2135, first Rust check at 2159).

Honest live scoping: contracts/live-evidence.json binds docs/checks/phase-27-live-attempt-05.json; tools/live_evidence.py:122-133 includes Cargo.lock in the runtime fingerprint, so the receipt is bound to the patched lockfile, and 313-315 requires the endpoint-profile limitation for phase 27/28 receipts. tools/red_team_management.py:792-819 requires a schemaVersion-2 read-only receipt and reconciles liveReceipt and liveVerified counts across all three ledgers; contracts/native-exports.json:54-62 reports liveVerified 1 of 3820 frozen capabilities.

Security and compatibility posture: crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:13484-13486 and 13600 redact Debug for both new types (and 13595-13597 for the builder); crates/scm-sdk/examples/directional_profiles.rs:50-57 proves lossless SecurityProfile responses for wrong-typed and null newly modeled fields under Mode::Response and Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults; CHANGELOG.md:17-28, docs/STABILITY.md:36-48, docs/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES.md:97-123 and docs/RESPONSE_DEFAULTS.md:48-51 disclose the intentional request tightening, the frozen tolerant response path, typed-over-extension precedence and the unchanged list default.

Governance and resume safety: tools/check_phase.py:318-354 builds the phase-27 set from cumulative phase-23 commands, drops package-consumer checks into phase 28, expands the tools/test_*.py glob to individual suites and reorders the dependency audit before the Rust matrix; tools/test_phase_checkpoint.py:41-50,84-96,127-143 rejects a changed phase, changed source, reordered commands, tampered receipts, stale/future checkpoints and later-command mutation; docs/PHASES.md:283-289 records the phase-27 acceptance boundary including the deliberate phase-28 deferral.
limitations: Read-only review: I could not run git, cargo or the phase driver, so exit codes, test counts, timestamps and source fingerprints come from docs/reviews/phase-27-chunk-wire-and-compatibility-attempt-05.checks.json rather than re-execution.
I recomputed no SHA-256. Parity-ledger sourceBindings, native-exports/qualification digests, the live receipt digest and the Cargo.lock hash rest on the recorded passing owner checks.

I did not verify that the 107 recorded commands are literally equal to commands_for(27); review_phase.check_evidence:215 enforces that equality at record time and the receipt reports passed true with all exit codes 0.

Directional create/update were never exercised against a tenant. The current receipt covers one OAuth token exchange and four 403 target-list probes on a non-default endpoint profile, and the docs now say so explicitly.

Clean extracted package-consumer builds are deliberately excluded from commands_for(27) (tools/check_phase.py:324; management_consumers reports executionClaimed false). That is phase 28 scope and I did not judge it.

I reviewed only the wire-and-compatibility chunk. Generated model and validation correctness was judged through both compilers, selected generated declarations (generated.rs:4464-4600, 13372-13604) and the independent oracle/fixture checks, not a full audit of models-and-validation.
I read neither .local/typescript nor any credential or tenant-registration material; contracts/sources/typescript-0.35.0 as pinned was treated as the authoritative upstream input.

The new request roots reject null/wrong-type values the old passthrough accepted. The plan authorizes this and CHANGELOG/STABILITY/DIRECTIONAL_PROFILES disclose it in both directions, so I treated it as a recorded maintainer decision, not a finding.
